Function reference

Movement

Speeds are from 0 (stopped) to 100 (full speed). Give a duration_ms and the robot stops by itself after that time; leave it out and the robot keeps going until you call stop().

bitbotXL.move_forward(speed=50, duration_ms=None)

Drive both wheels forward.

Parameters:

  • speed – Motor power from 0 (stopped) to 100 (full speed). Very low values may not be enough to turn the wheels. Default 50.

  • duration_ms – How long to drive, in milliseconds. The robot stops when the time is up and the function then returns. If None (the default) the function returns immediately and the robot keeps driving until stop() or another movement is called.

Example:

bot.move_forward(60, 2000)  # forward for 2 seconds, then stop
bitbotXL.move_backwards(speed=50, duration_ms=None)

Drive both wheels backwards.

Parameters:

  • speed – Motor power from 0 (stopped) to 100 (full speed). Default 50.

  • duration_ms – How long to drive, in milliseconds, before stopping. If None (the default) the robot keeps reversing until stop() or another movement is called.

Example:

bot.move_backwards(40, 500)  # reverse for half a second
bitbotXL.turn_left(speed=50, duration_ms=None)

Spin on the spot, anticlockwise (left wheel back, right wheel forward).

Parameters:

  • speed – Motor power from 0 (stopped) to 100 (full speed). Default 50.

  • duration_ms – How long to turn, in milliseconds, before stopping. If None (the default) the robot keeps turning until stop() or another movement is called. The angle turned depends on speed, duration and surface, so you will need to experiment.

Example:

bot.turn_left(50, 600)  # roughly a quarter turn on a smooth floor
bitbotXL.turn_right(speed=50, duration_ms=None)

Spin on the spot, clockwise (left wheel forward, right wheel back).

Parameters:

  • speed – Motor power from 0 (stopped) to 100 (full speed). Default 50.

  • duration_ms – How long to turn, in milliseconds, before stopping. If None (the default) the robot keeps turning until stop() or another movement is called.

Example:

bot.turn_right(50, 600)
bitbotXL.stop()

Stop both motors immediately.

Example:

bot.move_forward()   # no duration: keeps going
sleep(1000)
bot.stop()

LEDs

The BitBot has 12 RGB LEDs numbered 0 to 11: 0-5 on the left arm and 6-11 on the right arm. Functions with led (singular) control one LED by index; functions with leds (plural) control all of them.

Colours are (red, green, blue) tuples with each value from 0 to 255. These are built in: RED, GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW, PURPLE, WHITE.

bitbotXL.led_on(led, colour=(40, 40, 40))

Turn on a single LED, leaving the others unchanged.

The BitBot has 12 RGB LEDs: 0-5 on the left arm and 6-11 on the right. To control all of them at once use leds_on().

Parameters:

  • led – Which LED to light, 0 to 11.

  • colour – An (r, g, b) tuple, each value from 0 to 255. Use your own, e.g. (0, 50, 50), or a built-in: RED, GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW, PURPLE, WHITE. Default WHITE. Keep values low (under about 60) as the LEDs are very bright.

Example:

bot.led_on(0, bot.GREEN)    # first LED green
bot.led_on(11, (0, 0, 50))  # last LED blue
bitbotXL.led_off(led)

Turn off a single LED, leaving the others unchanged.

Parameters:

led – Which LED to turn off, 0 to 11.

Example:

bot.led_off(3)
bitbotXL.leds_on(colour=(40, 40, 40))

Turn on all 12 LEDs in the same colour.

Parameters:

colour – An (r, g, b) tuple, each value from 0 to 255, or a built-in colour such as RED. Default WHITE.

Example:

bot.leds_on(bot.RED)      # all LEDs red
bot.leds_on((0, 50, 50))  # all LEDs a custom colour
bitbotXL.leds_off()

Turn off all 12 LEDs.

Example:

bot.leds_off()

Buzzer

bitbotXL.buzzer(duration_ms=200)

Sound the buzzer at its fixed tone (about 2.4kHz).

The buzzer is a simple on/off type, so the pitch cannot be changed. The function waits until the beep has finished.

Parameters:

duration_ms – Length of the beep in milliseconds. Default 200.

Example:

bot.buzzer(500)  # half-second beep

Sensors

bitbotXL.get_distance(timeout_us=30000)

Measure the distance to the nearest object with the ultrasonic sensor.

Works best on hard, flat surfaces facing the sensor. Soft or angled objects may not reflect the sound back. Readings take up to about 30 ms, so don’t call it more often than every 50 ms or so.

Parameters:

timeout_us – How long to wait for the echo, in microseconds, before giving up. The default (30000) corresponds to about 5 m.

Returns:

The distance in centimetres as a whole number, or -1 if no echo was received (nothing in range, or the object reflected no sound).

Example:

if 0 <= bot.get_distance() < 15:
    bot.stop()   # something is closer than 15 cm
bitbotXL.get_left_light()

Read the left light sensor.

Returns:

A number from 0 (dark) to 1023 (very bright). Readings depend on the room lighting, so measure your own thresholds.

Example:

if bot.get_left_light() > bot.get_right_light():
    bot.turn_left(30)   # turn towards the light
bitbotXL.get_right_light()

Read the right light sensor.

Returns:

A number from 0 (dark) to 1023 (very bright).

Example:

print(bot.get_right_light())
bitbotXL.get_left_line()

Read the left line-following sensor (underneath the robot).

Returns:

1 means “over the line” 0 means “not over the line” or that something went wrong

Example:

on_line = bot.get_left_line() == 1
bitbotXL.get_right_line()

Read the right line-following sensor (underneath the robot).

Returns:

1 means “over the line” 0 means “not over the line” or that something went wrong

Example:

on_line = bot.get_right_line() == 1
